origin.description: Draw a series from an ARFIMA model.
origin.usage: fracdiff.sim(n, ar = NULL, ma = NULL, d, rand.gen = rnorm, innov = rand.gen(n + q, ...), n.start = NA, backComp = TRUE, mu = 0)

arguments.name: d
arguments.text: Fractional difference. It must lie in [-1/2, 1/2].

arguments.name: innov
arguments.text: The innovation series. It must have length at least n + q.

arguments.name: mu
arguments.text: Added to every point after the filter.

origin.details: The fractional part is the same recursion as the filter used by the likelihood. With the default burn-in and no autoregression, the first n points after a zero start are dropped. Pass innov so the series does not depend on R's generator.
origin.example: innov <- (1:8) / 10; cat(fracdiff.sim(8, d = 0.2, innov = innov, start.innov = numeric(0), n.start = 0, allow.0.nstart = TRUE)$series, "\n")

translation.description: Draw a series from an ARFIMA model.
translation.usage: fracdiff_sim(n, d, ar=None, ma=None, innov=None, n_start=None, back_comp=True, mu=0.0)

arguments.name: d
arguments.text: Fractional difference. It must lie in [-1/2, 1/2].

arguments.name: innov
arguments.text: The innovation series. It must have length at least n + q.

arguments.name: mu
arguments.text: Added to every point after the filter.

translation.details: The fractional part is the same recursion as the filter used by the likelihood. With the default burn-in and no autoregression, the first n points after a zero start are dropped. Pass innov so the series does not depend on R's generator.
translation.example: innov = [i / 10 for i in range(1, 9)]; print(fracdiff_sim(8, d=0.2, innov=innov, start_innov=[], n_start=0, allow_0_nstart=True)['series'])
